_: One node configuration per scenario. Drop the body into a PLUGIN node's 'configuration' with pluginId 'mongodb'. Every one names a secret rather than holding a password: store the value with the engine's secret management first. The connection fields are identical on all three node types, so they are shown once here and abbreviated afterwards.

_notes: Either connectionUri or host/port. A URI containing user:password@ is refused: split it as shown.
credentialId names both halves in the secret store as <id>.username and <id>.password; passwordSecret names the password alone.
Atlas requires TLS, which mongodb+srv:// turns on by itself.
The same node against Atlas. The SRV record supplies the hosts and the replica set; TLS is implied.
The database may live in the URI, or in 'database' where one node serves several.

insertCustomer._scenario: 1. Insert a customer, with form fields interpolated.
_notes: $date turns the resolved timestamp into a BSON date rather than a string, so range queries on it work.
A whole-value placeholder that resolves to a number is stored as a number: 'age' below arrives as an int.
ordered=false keeps going after a failure, which suits an import where one bad row should not stop the rest.

findCustomer._scenario: 2. Find one customer and map fields into workflow variables.
_notes: FIND_ONE publishes the document's own fields directly, so ${customer.name} works — as well as ${customer.document.name}.
'found' is false rather than an error when nothing matched: 'no such customer' is an ordinary outcome to branch on.

findManyPaged._scenario: Find a page of active adults, newest first.
_notes: hasMore is a fact, not a guess: the query asks for one more document than it returns.
includeTotalCount runs a second count over the same filter. Off unless a UI needs the total.

findByObjectId._scenario: Look a document up by its _id.
_notes: $oid is required. A 24-character hex string resolved from a variable stays a string on purpose, and a string never matches an ObjectId — the query is valid, runs, and returns nothing.
Update operators only. A plain document here is refused, because MongoDB would treat it as a replacement and drop every field it does not mention.
upsert inserts when the filter matched nothing, and publishes upsertedId.
confirmed is required: this touches every document the filter matches.
If the filter could resolve to {} — a variable that came back empty — it is refused separately unless allowEmptyFilter is set.
Every field the replacement does not contain is gone. That is why it is a separate operation and why it is confirmed.

deleteMany._scenario: Delete the documents a filter names.
_notes: confirmed is required, and an empty filter is refused on top of that.
Stages are validated before the server sees them: a stage missing its $ is caught here rather than as an unrecognised-field error several layers in.
allowDiskUse lets a large $group spill rather than failing at the server's in-memory stage limit.

distinctDepartments._scenario: Collect the distinct values of a field.

transaction._scenario: 5. A transaction: create a customer, debit an account and write an audit record, atomically.
_notes: One node, three operations. The transaction begins and ends inside it — see the README for why it cannot span workflow steps.
Needs a replica set or sharded cluster; a standalone server refuses it with MONGO_NOT_SUPPORTED.

Every write here is on one collection. Cross-collection atomicity needs the operations in one bulk write against a collection each, which this node cannot express: use it for the common case and a compensating node for the rest.

mongoToRestApi._scenario: 6. MongoDB → REST API. Read here, then feed the REST API node.
_notes: The read publishes items; the REST node interpolates them into its body as ${customers.items}.
Keep the page small: whatever this returns is held in memory and serialised into the next request.

mongoToDecision._scenario: 8. MongoDB → decision. Read, then branch on what came back.
_notes: 'found' and 'count' are published for exactly this: a decision node reads them without parsing a document.
expireAfterSeconds makes it a TTL index: the server deletes documents on its own schedule, with nothing in the workflow to record it.
partialFilterExpression indexes only the documents that match, which is how a unique index coexists with soft-deleted rows.

testConnection._scenario: 20. Prove a connection before a workflow depends on it.
_notes: Connects, pings and reports the server version without touching data. Run it on its own from the designer.
